outline: 550 The Derivative of a Linear Function

examples.solution_text:
The function is constant, so its graph is horizontal with gradient $0$ everywhere.
$f'(x)=0$

examples.question_text:
Find the derivative of each function.
(a) $f(x)=9-4x$
(b) $y=x$
(c) $g(x)=px+q$, where $p$ and $q$ are constants.
examples.solution_text:
A linear function's derivative is its gradient, the coefficient of $x$.
(a) $f'(x)=-4$
(b) $y'=1$
(c) $g'(x)=p$

Rewrite the function to identify its gradient.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=-\dfrac{5}{6}x+\dfrac{4}{3}\\f'(x)&=-\dfrac{5}{6}\end{align*}$

Expand to identify the coefficient of $x$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=15-10x\\f'(x)&=-10\end{align*}$

Expand and simplify to identify the gradient.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\dfrac{28}{3}-\dfrac{36x}{24}\\&=\dfrac{28}{3}-\dfrac{3}{2}x\\f'(x)&=-\dfrac{3}{2}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A bee flies straight from its hive to a flower $120$ m away in $15$ seconds at a constant speed. Find its speed.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Speed}&=\text{distance}\div\text{time}\\&=120\div15\\&=8\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$
This is the constant gradient of its distance–time graph.

Use the points $(0,30)$ and $(6,6)$.
$\begin{align*}m&=\dfrac{6-30}{6-0}\\&=\dfrac{-24}{6}\\&=-4\end{align*}$
The rate of change is $-4\text{ m/s}^2$.
The vertical intercept is $30$, so $v(t)=-4t+30$.

examples.derivation: Neither sqrt(7) nor 2/5 depends on x. Their sum is constant, so its graph is horizontal and f'(x)=0.
The coefficients of x are respectively -4, 1 and p. The constant terms do not affect the gradients, giving f'(x)=-4, y'=1 and g'(x)=p.
5(3-2x)=15-10x. The coefficient of x is -10, so f'(x)=-10.
(4/3)(7-9x/8)=28/3-36x/24=28/3-(3/2)x. Hence f'(x)=-3/2. The relation-led simplification continues an equation with an explicit left-hand side, so no phantom opening equals is required.
Constant speed is distance divided by elapsed time: 120/15=8 m/s. This equals the constant gradient of the distance–time graph.

The plotted points are (0,30), (2,22), (4,14) and (6,6). Each two-second increment decreases velocity by 8 m/s. Using the endpoints gives (6-30)/(6-0)=-4 m/s². The vertical intercept is 30 m/s, giving v(t)=-4t+30; this reproduces every plotted point.
